$doc: Live log (designed 2026-10-04): what a running batch is doing, step by step, and what a collector run, package install or Test run prints, live and afterwards. One view, LogLine rows; it opens in place of the screen it came from (‹ back). Batch frames are here; the collector frames are CollectorsLog in screens/collectors.json, placed in this row. Spec: docs/specs/live-log.md.

states.label: A · Queue: the batch card says what it is doing now (here: labeling one file of 22), and Show steps
B · Steps, live: labels are suggested one file at a time before Claude starts; the newest line is followed

D · Details on: the tool and what it touched under each step, never what it read or wrote
E · Review: Show steps next to the batch’s times
F · Steps after the run: checked by the vault core, waiting for your review
G · History → Jobs: a past batch’s steps, saved, through Applied and Found actions
H · 890 pt window: the same view, shorter step names; times stay on the right

boards.heading: Live log · a batch, step by step
boards.intro: “Is there any log that shows the progress of the batch?” A batch that started at 11:33 PM showed nothing until Claude’s first step at 11:37 PM: those four minutes were labels being suggested, one file at a time. Now the batch card on Queue says what is happening now, and Show steps opens the log in place of the screen (‹ goes back), from Queue while it runs, from Review, and from History → Jobs afterwards. Steps are plain words with a quiet mark (done, running, waiting, waiting for you, failed); repeats fold into one line you can open; the AI’s own status messages appear in its words. The log follows the newest line; scroll up and it stops, with Jump to latest. Details adds the raw line: the tool and what it touched, never contents. Copy takes the whole log as text. It stays after the run, kept with the job. Why in place and not a panel or a window: it works the same at 890 pt and in every screen (Collectors’ All runs and Activity already open this way), and the card on Queue keeps the one-line answer in view without opening anything.
